steps.title: Set up sterile workspace
steps.instruction: Perform all procedures for ESC culture and organoid generation in a Class II biosafety cabinet; place orbital shaker inside a humidified incubator set to 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Equilibrate plasticware and reagents
steps.instruction: Gather low‑attachment 96‑well plates, flasks, media supplements (e.g., B27) and tools; bring them to room temperature or pre‑warm to 37 °C as required before use.

steps.title: Prepare ESC medium
steps.instruction: Mix the following (pre‑warm to 37 °C where indicated) to a final volume of 50 mL: DMEM/F12‑Glutamax 43 mL, Sodium pyruvate 0.5 mL (1 mM), MEM NEAA 0.55 mL (1 mM), GlutaMax 0.5 mL (1 mM), β‑Mercaptoethanol 0.1 mL (0.1 mM), Fetal bovine serum 5 mL (10 %), Leukemia inhibitory factor 0.055 mL (1 × 10⁶ U mL⁻¹). Store FBS at –20 °C, all other reagents at 4 °C, and the complete medium at 4 °C for up to 1 month. Monitor phenol‑red colour (pink‑red acceptable; orange/yellow indicates acidification – discard).

steps.title: Prepare ESC cryopreservation medium
steps.instruction: Combine DMEM/F12‑Glutamax 40 mL, FBS 5 mL (10 %), DMSO 5 mL (10 %) to 50 mL total. Store DMSO at room temperature, FBS at –20 °C, DMEM at 4 °C; keep the complete freezing medium at 4 °C for up to 1 month. Aliquot 500 µL per cryovial, freeze gradually at –80 °C using a controlled‑rate container, then store long‑term at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare KSR medium for organoids
steps.instruction: To 50 mL total, add DMEM/F12‑Glutamax 44 mL, Sodium pyruvate 1 mL (1 mM), MEM NEAA 0.55 mL (0.1 mM), KnockOut™ serum replacement 5 mL (10 %), β‑Mercaptoethanol 0.114 mL (0.1 mM), IWP2 5 µL (2.5 µM). Prepare fresh under sterile conditions; store KSR at –20 °C, other components at 4 °C; discard after use.

steps.title: Prepare cortical maturation medium (CMM)
steps.instruction: Mix to 50 mL: DMEM/F12‑Glutamax 44 mL, GlutaMax 0.5 mL (1 mM), N‑2 supplement 0.5 mL (1 ×), NeuroCult™ SM1 (B27‑equivalent) 1 mL (1 ×). Store complete medium at 4 °C for up to 1 month.

steps.title: Prepare Mayer’s hematoxylin
steps.instruction: Dissolve in 1 L deionized water: Hematoxylin 1 g (0.1 %), Sodium iodate 0.2 g (0.02 %), Potassium alum 50 g (5 %), Chloral hydrate 50 g (5 %). Stir sequentially, filter, store at 20‑25 °C. Solution appears red‑violet and can be reused.

steps.title: Prepare eosin‑phloxine solution
steps.instruction: Prepare stock solutions: Eosin Y 1 g in 100 mL deionized water (1 %); Phloxine B 1 g in 100 mL deionized water (1 %). Mix 200 mL of the Eosin Y stock with 20 mL of the Phloxine B stock, add 1560 mL 95 % ethanol and 8 mL glacial acetic acid. Mix to homogeneity, filter, store at 20‑25 °C. Total volume ≈ 1788 mL.

steps.title: Prepare immunofluorescence buffers
steps.instruction: Permeabilization buffer: dissolve 0.5 g gelatin in 125 mL PBS (1 X), heat to 55 °C, add 0.625 mL Triton X‑100, filter, adjust pH to 7.4 with HCl. Store at 4 °C for ≤10 days. Citrate buffer: dissolve 2.1 g citric‑acid monohydrate in 1 L deionized water, adjust pH to 6 with 2 M NaOH; store at 4 °C. Washing buffer 2: dissolve 0.4 g CuSO₄ (10 mM) and 0.65 g NH₄Cl (50 mM) in 250 mL deionized water; store at 20‑25 °C, protect from light. 20X PBS: dissolve 29.25 g NaCl (137 mM), 4 g KCl (2.7 mM), 4.9 g K₂HPO₄ (2 mM), 8 g Na₂HPO₄·2H₂O (8 mM) in 1 L water, adjust to pH 7.3 with NaOH/HCl; dilute 1:20 to obtain 1× PBS. Store at 20‑25 °C.

steps.title: Coat flasks with gelatin
steps.instruction: Warm liquid gelatin at 37 °C for 10 min. Prepare 1 % gelatin (1 mL gelatin + 100 mL 1× PBS), filter through 0.22 µm (load slowly into a 25 mL syringe). Dilute to 0.1 % (5 mL 1 % gelatin + 45 mL PBS). Add 5 mL (T25) or 10 mL (T75) to cover the flask bottom. Incubate 30 min at 20‑25 °C, then remove excess gelatin before seeding.

steps.title: Thaw and seed ESCs
steps.instruction: Rapidly thaw frozen ESC vial at 37 °C with gentle swirling. Transfer cells to a 15 mL tube containing 5 mL pre‑warmed ESC medium, centrifuge 150 × g for 5 min (up to 250 × g acceptable). Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 10 mL ESC medium. After 30 min incubation, remove gelatin coating from the flask and add the cell suspension. Assess viability under an inverted microscope (phase‑bright, adherent colonies are healthy).

steps.title: Incubate ESCs and replace medium
steps.instruction: Incubate seeded flasks at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for ≥12 h. The next day, evaluate morphology and adherence; replace with fresh ESC medium (5 mL for T25, 10 mL for T75). Continue until ≥50 % confluency before any further manipulation.

steps.title: Passage ESCs
steps.instruction: Aspirate medium, wash cells twice with 1× PBS (remove FBS). Add 1 mL TrypLE, incubate 5 min at room temperature (or until cells detach). Neutralize with 9 mL DMEM + 10 % FBS, rinse to dislodge cells. Dilute the suspension 1:10–1:20 with fresh ESC medium depending on confluency. Return cells to the incubator (37 °C, 5 % CO₂).

steps.title: Cryopreserve ESCs
steps.instruction: When cultures reach 50‑70 % confluence, detach as in the passage step, centrifuge 150 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL pre‑cooled ESC freezing medium. Aliquot 500 µL into cryovials, place in a controlled‑rate freezing container, freeze gradually at –80 °C, then store long‑term at –80 °C.

steps.title: H&E staining of organoid sections
steps.instruction: Incubate deparaffinized slides in Mayer’s hematoxylin for 15 min; rinse in cold tap water for 10 min until blueing occurs. Incubate in eosin‑phloxine solution for 3 min; rinse in tap water for 3 min. Dehydrate sequentially: 96 % isopropanol 2 min, then 100 % isopropanol three washes of 2 min each, followed by xylene 3 min. Mount with Entellan and coverslip (polymerizes in ~20 min; no additional sealing needed).

steps.title: Antigen retrieval for IF
steps.instruction: Immerse slides in citrate buffer (pH 6.0) and heat in a steam/pressure (vapor) pot for 20 min. Allow slides to cool to 20‑25 °C before proceeding.

steps.title: Block and permeabilize sections
steps.instruction: Wash slides twice in 1× PBS for 2 min each. Draw a hydrophobic barrier around each section (≈100–200 µL capacity). Apply permeabilization buffer containing 5 % BSA; dilute 5 % BSA with the buffer to obtain a 1 % BSA solution for blocking. Incubate as needed (typically 10 min) at room temperature.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Prepare primary antibodies diluted in 1 % BSA in 1× PBS (use dilutions from Table 1). Add to each slide, cover with the hydrophobic barrier, and incubate ≥12 h at 4 °C in a humidified chamber.

steps.title: Post‑primary washes and permeabilization
steps.instruction: Wash slides twice in 1× PBS for 2 min each. Apply permeabilization buffer for 10 min, then drain.

steps.title: Secondary antibody and nuclear staining
steps.instruction: Add fluorophore‑conjugated secondary antibody diluted in 1 % BSA in 1× PBS; incubate 1 h at room temperature in the dark. Wash twice in 1× PBS for 2 min each. Prepare Hoechst solution by diluting 2 µL Hoechst in 40 mL 1× PBS (1 : 20 000); incubate slides 5 min in the dark. Wash twice in 1× PBS for 2 min each.

steps.title: Final washes, mounting and storage
steps.instruction: Incubate slides with Washing buffer 2 for 10 min in the dark, then briefly rinse with deionized water. Mount with Shandon™ Immo‑Mount, avoiding air bubbles; the medium polymerizes within ~20 min. No additional sealing required.

description: All procedures for cultivating embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and generating murine cerebral organoids (COs) must be performed under sterile conditions in a Class II biological safety cabinet. Organoid culture requires an orbital shaker placed in a humidified incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2. This protocol employs the E14tg2a mouse ESC line (derived from 129/Ola mouse blastocysts).⁠1 These cells are pluripotent and efficiently differentiate toward neuroectodermal lineages under defined, serum-free culture conditions. Before starting, prepare all media and reagents as listed in “materials and equipment”. Some reagents can be prepared in advance and stored as indicated; others must be freshly prepared immediately before use. Complete information, including catalog numbers and storage conditions, is provided in the key resources table. Ensure that all culture plasticware (e.g., low-attachment 96-well plates), media supplements (e.g., B27), and handling tools are available and equilibrated to room temperature or 37°C as appropriate. Accurate timing, consistent cell handling, and gentle pipetting during embryoid body (EB) formation are critical for reproducibility and organoid viability.
